chunk_findings.detail: The fix only stops a same-holder/different-tree lease from being treated as “mine” when `bound` is True. `_tree_bound` is True only if `here` is the worktree of a live, unfinished lease. So if the commit happens in a tree whose own lease has lapsed (and is therefore absent from `unfinished_leases`), `bound` is False and the old bug remains: a live lease I hold for a different worktree still counts as mine by holder match. Concrete input: live lease B has `holder == me`, `worktree = W_B`, `globs = ["b/**"]`; commit runs in lapsed tree `W_A` touching `b/file.py`. `_tree_bound(W_A)` returns False, `_counts_as_mine(B)` returns True, so `_split_leases` puts `b/**` in `mine`, and the hook allows/lists B’s globs from the wrong tree. The same failure also occurs for any non-live owned tree, such as a main checkout not represented in `unfinished_leases`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/enforce.py:_counts_as_mine

chunk_findings.detail: The hook now computes `bound = _tree_bound(...)` and passes it to `_split_leases` and `_with_contested`, but the `_expired_you_hold` call below the shown hunk is unchanged and still uses the new parameter’s default `False`. As a result, the lapsed-lease path does not apply the new classification: when `here` is bound to a live lease, a lapsed lease I hold for a *different* tree can still be reported as “would have been mine” / “claim X” using the old holder-only test, even though the added parameter exists precisely to apply the same bound-aware test there.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/enforce.py:_expired_you_hold

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts `E.check_commit(repo, cfg, agent="owner") == (0, "")` when T1 is bound to the current worktree with glob `src/*`, and the same holder also has T2 with no worktree leasing `docs/x.md`. That preserves the bug this change is meant to fix: the commit is in T1's tree, so the hook must judge it by T1's lease, and T2 is still "another item of the same holder"—its no-tree lease should not cover a different item's tree. If the implementation satisfies this assertion by treating an empty tree bound as matching every tree, then Bc57d0b031a still occurs whenever the committing agent also holds an additional no-tree item whose glob matches the edited path. The no-tree fallback is only defensible when the current checkout is not some other item's tree (the third test), not when it is T1's tree.

chunk_findings.detail: `_tree_bound` is defined but never called anywhere in this diff, and the new `bound` parameters on `_split_leases`, `_with_contested`, and `_expired_you_hold` all keep `False` as their default. No production call site is updated to compute `bound = _tree_bound(...)` and pass it, so the new classification is dead code. Concrete input: unfinished lease A owns worktree W_A; unfinished lease B has `holder == me`, `worktree = W_B`, `globs = ["src/*"]`; the commit runs in W_A and touches `src/x.md`, which only B covers. `check_commit` still calls `_split_leases(repo, state, cfg, me, W_A, now)` with `bound=False`, so `_counts_as_mine(repo, B, me, W_A, False)` returns `B.holder == me` and merges B’s globs into `mine`; the commit is allowed from the wrong tree. The same missing caller update leaves the lapsed-lease path on `bound=False`, so previous findings 1 and 2 still hold in effect.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/enforce.py:_tree_bound

chunk_findings.detail: The version still uses holder-only matching whenever `_tree_bound(repo, state, cfg, here, now)` returns `False`. A tree with no lease at all gives `bound=False`, even when the lease being classified is bound to a different worktree. Concrete input: worktrees `T1` and `W_B`; agent `me` holds a live unfinished lease on `W_B` with glob `docs/*`; no lease in `state` has `worktree == T1`. Commit in `T1` touches `docs/x.md`. `_tree_bound(T1, now)` is `False`, so `_split_leases(... bound=False)` passes the `W_B` lease to `_counts_as_mine`, which matches by `holder == me` and puts it in `mine`; no uncovered paths remain and the hook returns `Verdict(OK, "")`. A lease bound to ANOTHER tree still covers a commit in `T1`, which is the bug this change is meant to prevent. The lapsed-current-lease case was fixed by making `_tree_bound` count lapsed leases, but the unleased-tree case is not.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/enforce.py:_counts_as_mine (called from `check_commit`)

chunk_findings.detail: The test asserts `E.check_commit(repo, cfg, agent="owner") == (0, "")` when T1 is bound to the current worktree with glob `src/*` and the same holder also has T2 with `worktree=""` leasing `docs/x.md`, then stages `docs/x.md` in T1's tree. This preserves the original same-holder/different-item bug for holders who have a no-tree item: a "helper" item with no tree can still cover files in another item's worktree. Concrete input: owner holds T1 in tree A for `src/*`, and T2 with no tree for `docs/x.md`; a commit of `docs/x.md` in tree A passes, even though tree A is T1's item tree and T1 does not lease that file. The "by design" note in the triage is the bypass, not a refutation: only leases bound to ANOTHER tree are excluded, so a lease bound to NO tree is still treated as cover-anywhere.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_hook_you_hold_identity.py:test_a_holders_item_without_a_tree_still_covers_its_commit_here

chunk_findings.detail: The test expects a lease bound to T1's worktree to cover a commit made in the primary checkout `repo`, which the test itself says is "no item's tree." Since T1 does have a tree, a commit outside that tree is not a commit in T1's tree, and T1's lease should not be the lease judging it; otherwise the worktree/branch binding on the lease is ignored whenever the cwd is not a leased worktree. Concrete input: `_setup` leases T1 for `src/*` in its own linked worktree (with its own branch); the test stages `src/other.py` in `repo` and asserts the commit passes. If the primary checkout is on a different branch, this is the same wrong-tree conflation the module docstring says the change fixes.

chunk_findings.detail: [r-lock-cycle-selfheal] The new test explicitly encodes the forbidden “hold while waiting” pattern: WAITER holds a lease on T4 (`A.claim(repo, "T4", no_worktree=True, agent=WAITER)`) and then poll-waits on T2 while this change keeps that hold alive. The recorded rule says agents never poll-wait or hold while waiting, and the change hardens that pattern instead of using the desired `needs` edges to avoid the circular wait (e.g. WAITER holds T4 while HOLDER holds T1, and each waits for the other's item). Keeping the lease alive here creates the very undetected circular wait the rule prioritizes preventing.

chunk_findings.detail: The renewal check is only made after `time.sleep(min(poll, left))`, so the actual maximum lease-renewal gap is `poll`, not the `heartbeat_s` interval promised by `_keep_alive`. Given `lease.heartbeat_s=1` and an `A.wait(..., timeout_s=4, poll_s=5, agent=WAITER)`, `keep_alive()` is not called until t=4, so the first T4 renewal happens at 4s despite a 1s heartbeat. The new test hides this by using `poll_s=0.2 < heartbeat_s=1`; with `poll_s > heartbeat_s` the waiter’s own lease can still lapse during the wait, which is exactly the bug this change claims to fix.

The offered refusal “wait takes no new hold” does not answer the rule: [r-lock-cycle-selfheal] forbids holding a lease while waiting at all, independent of when the hold was taken, and calls for `needs` edges instead. This diff hardens and enshrines the forbidden pattern rather than removing it.

chunk_findings.detail: The new lease-wait path is dead: `_judge` / `_judge_lease` are defined and `wait(..., lease=...)` accepts `lease`, but the polling loop in `wait` never calls the new `_judge` dispatcher (the diff changes `_wait_globs` but leaves the pre-existing judge call that produces `v` untouched). Given `wait(repo, lease="bob")` with no `item`/`globs`, while `bob` holds a lease and some unrelated item is ready, this still runs the normal any-item judge and returns that ready item instead of blocking until Bob's lease is free, so the advertised lease wait does not work.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/wait.py:wait

chunk_findings.detail: The expected `Param` for `lease` in `test_command_registry.py` sets `help` to `"...covers it); a bare wait returns the first ready item at once"` (semicolon, no trailing period), but the actual declared parameter in `ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle.py` defines `help="...covers it). A bare wait returns the first ready item at once."` (period after the parenthesis and trailing period) and a separate `cli_help` with the semicolon string. The registry test will fail as written because the expected `help` value does not match the actual `Param.help` value.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_command_registry.py:169 (lease Param)

chunk_findings.detail: This test explicitly relies on a polling wait: `A.wait(..., poll_s=0.2)` while `agent-waiter` is blocked on a lease held by `agent-holder`. That is the polling wait [r-lock-cycle-selfheal] says agents must never do; waits should be resolved by adding needs edges, not by sleeping and re-checking. The test encodes the forbidden behavior as accepted.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_wait_lease_target.py:55

chunk_findings.detail: The fixture makes `lease="src/*.py"` match both the held `src/a.py` and the already-ready `src/unrelated.py`. A buggy `A.wait` that wrongly returns `woke=True` as soon as any ready item matches the lease glob would satisfy `assert out.data["woke"]` immediately, before `release()` runs. The test therefore does not actually require the holder release to be the wake trigger, which is the behavior it is named for.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_wait_lease_target.py:test_wait_on_a_file_wakes_when_the_holder_releases

chunk_findings.detail: The new lease-wait logic is never wired into `wait()`. The diff adds `_judge` and `_judge_lease`, but `wait()` only uses the new `lease` argument for `_wait_globs` and `_ready_advice`; it never calls `_judge`. Concrete failure: `wait(repo, lease="holder")` where `holder` still has a live lease on `held.txt`, while some unrelated item `README` is ready. Because the polling loop still takes the no-item `_judge_any` path, it returns `ready` for `README`, and `_ready_advice(v, lease)` then reports `holder is free of other agents' leases`, even though `holder` still holds `held.txt`. The lease wait is not performed at all.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/wait.py:wait

chunk_findings.detail: If the lease target is the caller's own agent id, `_judge` filters out every lease whose `holder == me` before calling `_judge_lease`. Given `_judge(st, cfg, me="agent-7", item="", phase="", kind="", want=None, repo=repo, lease="agent-7")` while `agent-7` holds a live lease on `x`, `_judge_lease` receives an `others` dict with none of `agent-7`'s leases, so `held` is empty and it returns `"status": "ready"`. That violates the documented lease condition “agent id … ready once it holds nothing.”
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/lifecycle/wait.py:_judge

chunk_findings.detail: `test_wait_on_a_file_wakes_when_the_holder_releases` only asserts `out.data["woke"]` after scheduling a 1-second delayed `A.release`. The fixture already has T9 ready with glob `src/unrelated.py`, which matches the lease glob `"src/*.py"`. If the lease-wake logic is wrong and returns `woke=True` immediately for any matching unheld path, this test still passes because T9 is unheld but matched; it never verifies that `A.wait` was actually blocked while `HOLDER` still held `src/a.py`. A first check with `timeout_s=0` on the same `"src/*.py"` glob expecting `not out.data["woke"]` would catch that defect.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_wait_lease_target.py:61
